title: API Gateway Integration Latency for Serverless Backends

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `aws:cloudwatch` events with `namespace="AWS/ApiGateway" metric_name="IntegrationLatency"` into `index=aws`. Confirm UC-4.5.14 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `aws:cloudwatch` traffic without `namespace="AWS/ApiGateway" metric_name="IntegrationLatency"`. Confirm UC-4.5.14 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:cloudwatch` collected via `Splunk_TA_aws`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch" namespace="AWS/ApiGateway" metric_name="IntegrationLatency"

description: UC-4.5.14 — API Gateway Integration Latency for Serverless Backends: queries AWS `aws:cloudwatch` for search criteria `namespace="AWS/ApiGateway" metric_name="IntegrationLatency"` and returns actor, resource, and region context for performance review and change validation.
value: On AWS, detecting 'API Gateway Integration Latency for Serverless Backends' early shortens cloud incident response and produces defensible audit evidence for identity and change-management controls. UC-4.5.14 drives medium-priority performance alerting before customer-impacting drift.
implementation: Enable detailed CloudWatch metrics for REST or HTTP APIs. Ingest `IntegrationLatency` alongside `Latency` and `4XXError`/`5XXError`. Split dashboards by stage (prod vs dev). Alert when integration latency exceeds backend SLA or diverges from total API latency (pointing to edge vs origin issues).

knownFalsePositives: This pattern can surge during change windows, in sandboxes, and when a platform is in maintenance, so we line alerts up with the calendar and take a second look before we call it an incident.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_aws` with the modular input for `aws:cloudwatch`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.5.16.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `metric_name` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Enable detailed CloudWatch metrics for REST or HTTP APIs. Ingest `IntegrationLatency` alongside `Latency` and `4XXError`/`5XXError`. Split dashboards by stage (prod vs dev). Alert when integration latency exceeds backend SLA or diverges from total API latency (pointing to edge vs origin issues).
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch" namespace="AWS/ApiGateway" metric_name="IntegrationLatency"
| table _time metric_name namespace unit average maximum
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.5.14_api_gateway_integration_14"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:cloudwatch` in `index=aws` to detect api gateway integration latency for serverless backends. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the Amazon CloudWatch console Metrics for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `metric_name` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_5_14_alert` with severity aligned to `medium` criticality. Dashboard: Line chart (IntegrationLatency vs Latency by API), Heatmap (route/method if dimensions available), Table (ApiName, Stage, p95 integ_ms)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_aws` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
